text:
Bitcoin sustained its recovery above $63,000 on June 20, briefly breaching $64,000 before consolidating. The asset remains within a highly leveraged derivatives decision zone amid macroeconomic headwinds. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs continue bleeding assets following a historic 13-day outflow streak that erased roughly $4.33 billion, as institutions adopt defensive postures.

Regulatory activity is accelerating globally. In the U.S., crypto firms are pushing for the Crypto Clarity Act to secure developer protections, while lawmakers filed a bipartisan bill delaying retail CBDC implementation until 2030. Simultaneously, the ECB is lobbying against offshore exchange expansion ahead of full MiCA enforcement.

The broader risk-asset complex remains constrained by a hawkish Federal Reserve. Although equities rebounded on a U.S.-Iran agreement that eased energy prices, the 2-year Treasury yield surged to 4.20% and the DXY approaches one-year highs. This resilient dollar and elevated short-end yield environment continues to suppress the attractiveness of non-yielding digital assets.
